➢Pro-fit/Managerial Round (9th August, TPO)

Online Assessment :
The online assessment consisted of three coding questions: the initial one being easy,
followed by a medium-level question, and concluding with another easy-level question.
1.
Power Limit : Given two variables, A and B, representing power levels, the task is
to determine the maximum time until either A or B reaches a power level of 0.
There's a condition and an operation to be applied to the chosen power variable.
The approach involves selecting the variable with the highest current power
using Heap and extending the time based on this choice.
10 out of 10 test cases pass.

2
2.
Auto Complete : Extension of Edit Distance problem on Leetcode (Edit Distance
- Leetcode) . Some simple implementation after counting minimum changes for
every word with respect to a Sample word .
Implemented a recursive approach, all test cases were not passed.
2D DP grid was expected.
8 out of 10 test cases pass.
words = [ “tocor” , “torect” , “tocfrrec” , “tocorre” , “tocofecd” ]
Sample word: “tocorrect”
3.
Backlinks Sorting : Two arrays, namely WebPage and Backlinks were given.
Each webpage possessed an associated backlink score. The task involved
arranging the webpages in descending order based on their respective backlink
scores. To accomplish this, I utilized Python defaultdict, to establish a mapping
between backlink scores and webpages. The approach taken was characterized
by its ease of implementation, rendering it a straightforward sorting problem.
10 out of 10 test cases pass.
Interview Rounds :
1.
Technical Round I : During the initial introduction, I emphasized on Problem
Solving and Data Structures & Algorithms.
Overview regarding my projects was asked, I described both projects within 5-6
minutes.
As my resume included information about my rankings in Leetcode Weekly
Contests, the conversation naturally shifted in that direction.
The interviewer inquired about easy/basic Linked List problems, expecting me
to both explain the concepts and provide code implementations.
Implementation of adding a node, deleting it was asked and its code was
expected.
Later, I attempted to guide the interview towards more advance DSA concepts
such as AVL Trees, KMP algorithm, Binary Lifting, and Disjoint Sets for Graphs
but it didn’t work out.
A significant portion of the interview revolved around exploring the practical
utilization of data structures in specific scenarios.
Next few minutes were spent on questions of OOPS and DBMS.
In the OOPS domain, questions involving virtual functions, implementing copy
constructors, abstraction, inheritance, and certain Yes/No inquiries were asked.
In DBMS, Normalisation, ER Model was asked.

3
Technical Round I ended with 2 SQL query questions, I solved both of them in 3
distinct approaches.
I would recommend, take time & then answer, in order to avoid an
extended chain of consecutive questions.
2.
Technical Round II : During the intro, I highlighted my accomplishments and
rankings in Weekly and Biweekly Leetcode Contests.
As my branch was EXTC , the interview focused extensively on concepts related
to Computer Networks (CN).
In CN, topics such as the OSI Model, TCP, UDP, various routing protocols, IP and
MAC addresses, DNS, as well as questions related to circuit switching and packet
switching were asked.
Discussion randomly turned towards File Transfer Protocol, HTTP, http get, http
post, RAM ROM, cache.
Finally the Interviewer started with DSA questions, implementation of Queue,
Dequeue was asked.
This was followed by a Medium-Hard level DSA question involving Linked Lists.
Specifically, the problem was an extension of the Detect Cycle in LL and
Remove Cycle problem found on LeetCode (Leetcode LL Cycle). The task
required a three-step approach for a final solution.
Que . Even number of nodes, cycle from last node to first node. The desired
response entailed pairs of n/2 nodes, each forming a loop from the second node
to the first for every pair.
Ans:
First Step: Initially, employing the Slow and Fast pointers to detect and
subsequently remove the loop.
Second Step: Splitting the linked list into partitions enabled by the loop removal,
with a temporary pointer designated for the next partition.
Third Step: Linking the fast pointer's next to the forementioned temporary
pointer for each pair, thereby achieving the desired outcome.
Upon detailed discussion of the approach, I was prompted to code the solution,
which I executed using three distinct functions. Throughout this process, I
elucidated each step and the functionality of every function, leaving a positive
impression on the interviewer.

4
Some questions were asked on OOPS : Diamond problem, Inheritance,
Interfaces, etc. Technical Round II ended with DBMS questions on A.C.I.D.
properties, Primary key, Foreign Key.
I tried to steer the interview towards topics/concepts where I held
particular strengths & it proved beneficial.
3.
Pro-Fit/Manegerial Round: This interview round lasted 30 minutes. I was asked
to explain my projects in detail.
I took approximately 10 minutes to thoroughly expound upon the various
features of the projects, accompanied by a logical breakdown of their
implementations.
I was asked about my Internship followed by my experience as an Admission
Counsellor for exams like JEE, NEET.
Furthermore, there was a brief exploration of the Database Management
Architecture of the Whatsapp Application, it covered the fundamental aspects of
the application's database structure.
This interview round ended and the interviewer was overall satisfied with the
answers.
4. HR Round: Behavioral questions regarding pressure management were asked.
Additionally, there were questions related to my internship experience, including
an exploration of the lessons gleaned from the internship. Fundamental
questions, such as the motivation behind desiring to work at DB was asked.
The interviewer further inquired regarding my problem-solving approach,
marking the conclusion of the Human Resources round.
Final Verdict : Selected
Job Role: Graduate Analyst, Deutsche Bank Operations India.
Date: 9 August 2023
Develop a comprehensive understanding of the subjects that align with your
areas of interest. In my case, I dedicated my attention towards Problem
Solving & Data Structures and Algorithms, which significantly contributed to
my successful navigation through the interview rounds, even in the absence of
any prior preparation.
Direct your attention toward Computer Science fundamentals, ensuring a
foundational understanding of the relevant aspects of the job role.

5
The TPO Department of the institute played a pivotal role in ensuring a seamless
overall placement process. Their continuous assistance and support throughout
the placement journey were highly commendable. The TPO coordinators and
representatives (CRs) were readily available at every step, effectively managing
and providing guidance to students, thus contributing significantly to the
success of the placement process.
